outcome.technical: ONE LOCK, ONE HELPER: every plan-file write in _evidence_io (pointer, record, reconcile, evidence boundary) goes through write_plan_file(project, path, change, note, session_id, wait, outcome, repair, config) under SHARD_LOCK='index' - the lock every audit-task verb (_under_lock), the panel (_panel_write.LOCK_NAME) and close-phase take - reading the file only after the acquire; lk1/lk2/lk3 hold it by AST. The phase lock is NOT taken: it claims a phase's run and guards no write, and one lock leaves no order to keep. It is one lock per PLAN, not per shard: every plan-file write excludes every other; measured on a copy of this repo's plan (373 KB index, 336 KB P169 shard), two rounds 50 s apart: solo hold 99-121 ms; a wave of three started together 122-431 ms per member, of six at most 845/824 ms; every record landed, so a wave of three cannot reach RECORD_WAIT_SECONDS (30 s) on this machine; a member waiting past it exits 3 with its ledger row written. Lock behaviour: a record waits RECORD_WAIT_SECONDS for a live holder, then exits 3 green or red; pointer/reconcile/boundary wait WAIT_SECONDS; a verb behind a record waits its own WAIT_SECONDS (unchanged); a dead holder is never taken over and the refusal says what happened, then audit-lock.py release index --force, then the re-run; a held phase lock refuses nothing any more. REPEATS: repeat_carried/record_carrying carry repeatedRun and the steps from the ledger row, else from the replaced record under the lock, else repeatedRunUnread {runId, basis}; a reader asks repeatedRun first; a whole repeat has no startedAt and its own durationMs/selectionMs (schema, guide, conventions say the same). reconcile rewrites lastRun from a newer ledger row in the pointer's write. Text: --record help and E_UNRECORDED comment say green or red; the unrecorded line names the index lock. Group sign-off (audit-task.py _group_record) now carries the repeated run when the ledger or plan holds it (grc1-grc3). DRIVE BOUND (finding P169-R30): cancelled_gate in drive-phase.py is the one decision for the task gate and the phase gate; the count is the launch mark's cancelledBefore, carried when a relaunch replaces the mark, gone when a verdict spends it; CANCELLED_BOUND = 2 (UNMEASURED_BOUND's count, for its reason); below it the gate is relaunched under a new token with no attempt spent, at it the drive asks gate-cancelled (rerun|block) or phase-gate-cancelled (rerun|decline), and the ask stays open; rerun drops the mark (count from zero), block blocks with the reason. bg4 now pins dispatch-again under a new token (its wait arm deleted: the killed run's record now lands, so wait cannot be reached), cb1-cb7 the bound. Dependants: wait-gate read-back reads the cancelled record; each cancelled run's stages are appended once by its own record write (record_stages excludes only repeats), which is right since each ran; a resumed session whose gate was SIGTERMed counts one on the first next, a SIGKILLed gate leaves no record and stays wait-gate as before; a wave member's mark and parked ask are its own, so the bound is per member (not tested in a wave fixture); --explain prints the decide text with no run: line (cb1); a loop on next --signal sees `audit P1 ask P1.1 | gate-cancelled: ... | next: next P1 --signal --answer rerun|block ...` with no run: line, the same on every call, so it ends only if it stops on a non-dispatch verb; auto ends at the ask instead of relaunching (the relaunch's new token had defeated AUTO_REPEAT_BOUND). orchestrator.md names one sibling ask in a pointer sentence to execute-task.md (which now carries gate-cancelled); it is not an enumeration and has 13 bytes left under measure-context's ceiling, so no row was added; measure-context --gate unchanged from HEAD (GATE OK, every figure identical). Docs: CHANGELOG, COMPATIBILITY, guide, manifest-conventions, schema, README (an invariant row and the refused-record paragraph), doctor.md, panel.md, execute-task.md, verbs-in-full.md, handbook.html, _panel_runstate.py comment; gen-demo-manifest exemption row. One rewrite of write_evidence_since in _evidence_io.py was made through a Bash python script rather than the Edit tool. Mutations (scratch export, landing confirmed, pycache purged, restored, cmp clean): 18 rows all killed - lock is phase lock alone; read before lock in helper/record/pointer/reconcile; wait=0; copied steps emptied; reconcile writes no record; save outside helper; group copy without source; record_carrying ignores ledger; help says green only; cancel count never carried (task, phase); bound never reached; bound reached at once (allow); count survives a verdict; rerun keeps the mark. Runs: task gate 3/3 files ok 2366 cases; test_drive_phase alone 1039 ok; extra suites 6/6 ok 1005; test__panel_runstate 44 ok; check-rendered-artifacts --before-commit 0, check-example-ledgers 0, check-git-pipeline 0; measure-context --gate OK; full sweep 198/198 files ok, 19367 cases. Gate timing --record before/after: 472/263 ms vs 215/222 ms (round one before was a cold start).
outcome.descriptive: A gate's record and a verb's write of one plan file no longer lose each other, a repeated verdict's record says where its steps came from, and a gate that keeps being killed stops the drive with an ask instead of looping.
